The map's label for small chiefdoms and trading kingdoms in Borneo, the Philippines and nearby islands between 800 and 1200. Indian religion, writing and titles reached them through trade. Most are known from scattered finds rather than written histories.

What survives:

  • The Laguna Copperplate Inscription of 900, the oldest known document from the Philippines, records the cancelling of a debt and names a place called Tondo.
  • The Butuan boats, large plank boats found in Mindanao. Butuan sent envoys to Song China in 1001.
  • Gold work, such as a golden image of a Hindu Buddhist goddess found in Agusan.
  • In eastern Borneo, the much older Yupa inscriptions of Kutai show Indian style kingship there from about 400.

Rulers took titles such as rajah and datu. The great power to the west was Srivijaya on Sumatra. The map's label for the same area in the 1300s is minor Hindu and Buddhist kingdoms.
